title: Shiba duality and $η$-altermagnetism: Pairing and charge orders in bipartite attractive Hubbard models
abstract: We show that Shiba duality maps the altermagnetic principle of momentum-dependent band splitting from spin to $η$-pseudospin, defining $η$-altermagnetism ($η$-ALM) as a Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) counterpart of ALM in pairing and charge orders. In half-filled pure Hubbard models on bipartite lattices, the duality relates repulsion-driven antiferromagnetism (AFM) to attraction-driven $η$-AFM with uniform singlet pairing and staggered charge-density modulation. In the BdG bands, the Shiba-dual parity-time-reversal $\mathcal{\tilde{P}}\mathcal{\tilde{T}}$ symmetry protects a Kramers degeneracy of $η$-pseudospin. Anisotropic second-neighbor hopping breaks this degeneracy and generates $η$-ALM. Odd-parity $η$-ALM shows $η$-pseudospin splitting, whereas even-parity $η$-ALM has spin-$η$-locked splitting. Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov computations on checkerboard and honeycomb lattices find $η$-ALMs with $p$-, $d$-, and $f$-wave splitting structures. Possible generalizations and experimental probes are discussed.
summary: This work develops the concept of $\eta$-altermagnetism by applying Shiba duality to map spin-based Altermagnetism principles onto charge and pairing orders. Using BdG theory on attractive Hubbard models, the authors predict specific $\eta$-pseudospin splitting patterns that arise from symmetry breaking due to lattice hopping anisotropies.
main_problem: The paper investigates $\eta$-altermagnetism ($\eta$-ALM) as a generalization of Altermagnetism (ALM) to pairing and charge orders in attractive Hubbard models.
main_result: Shiba duality establishes an exact correspondence between repulsion-driven Antiferromagnetism (AFM) and attraction-driven $\eta$-AFM, leading to observable $\eta$-pseudospin splitting structures like $p$-, $d$-, or $f$-wave patterns.
method: The study employs mean-field Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) theory combined with Shiba duality mapping techniques.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the pure Hubbard Hamiltonian on bipartite lattices, analyzed at half-filling using both spin and $\eta$-pseudospin order parameters.
key_observables: Onsite charge order ($s_{\mu}^i$), onsite spin order ($\sigma_{\mu}^2$), onsite pairing order ($p_{\mu}^i$), and the resulting $\eta$-pseudospin splitting energies in band structures.
important_parameters: Half-filling ($n_f=1$), attractive interaction strength (related to $U_0 < 0$), and hopping anisotropies (e.g., second-neighbor hopping).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations within the BdG formalism, assuming intrinsic particle-hole symmetry for certain analyses.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $\eta$-ALMs on checkerboard and honeycomb lattices, showing ground-state orders (CDM and USP), resulting band splitting patterns, and BZ mappings of these energies.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the connection via Shiba duality between spin ALM and $\eta$-ALM. It then details the BdG formalism for calculating charge/pairing orders and analyzes how anisotropic hopping breaks symmetry to generate measurable $\eta$-pseudospin splitting in momentum space.
why_interesting: It extends concepts of magnetic ordering (ALM) into superconducting/charge sectors using a novel pseudospin degree of freedom ($\eta$), which is relevant for understanding exotic pairing symmetries in strongly correlated superconductors.
